newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's centre-left PPI party for talks with right.
newsitem.headline: Italy's centre-left PPI party for talks with right.

text.p: The leader of Italy's Popular party, part of the centre-left government, said on Wednesday that overtures from the centre-right on a deal over budgetary measures needed for EMU should be explored.

PPI Party secretary Franco Marini also told the daily Corriere della Sera newspaper in an interview that Prime Minister Romano Prodi should give less space to the demands of the hardline leftists of Communist Refoundation.

"Why not investigate fully the willingness of the opposition?" Marini asked, referring to suggestions that the centre-left and centre-right should reach an agreement to ensure the country is in shape to join a single European currency.
"I don't see why the government should not, as far as possible, involve the opposition in parliament."
Massimo d'Alema, leader of the main Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), called for a show of "common responsibility" at the weekend and generosity from the centre-right opposition.
Centre-right Freedom Alliance leader Silvio Berlusconi has offered Prodi a deal in cuts on welfare spending in return for support over measures needed to qualify for EMU.

The government easily won a confidence vote on Tuesday to sweep aside opposition amendments to the final part of its 1997 austerity budget. A second confidence vote on a decree for the transport sector was due later on Wednesday.
Communist Refoundation, an ally that is not part of the government, voted with the centre-left coalition but warned that it considered further belt-tightening unnecessary.
The government is working on a new mini-budget which will focus on structural changes.
Analysts expect it to include up to 15 trillion lire ($9 billion) of deficit cuts and many have urged Prodi to prune welfare spending -- especially the generous state pensions system.

Marini warned that the government must avoid "old experiences". He said the centre-left Olive Tree bloc should first reach agreement with the government and the government should then negotiate with Refoundation. ($ = 1665 Italian Lire)
